description: We’re a team of five building Fit for Mars, an offline app that helps astronauts fight muscle loss on the way to Mars.
summary:
Fit for Mars helps people on long journeys to Mars, from professional astronauts to
future civilian crews, prevent muscle loss on their own. In microgravity, people can lose
up to 20% of their muscle mass, and the lower legs are hit hardest. Today, muscle data
goes to specialists on Earth; on the way to Mars, a communication delay of up to 20
minutes makes that impossible.
Our app measures individual muscles with segmental bioelectrical impedance (BIA) and

body part is compared with the person's own baseline, set after the first two weeks to

the device.
details:
Fit for Mars is an offline app that helps people on long journeys to Mars, from

professional astronauts to future civilian crews, prevent muscle loss on their own.

The problem: in microgravity, people can lose up to 20% without exercise, and the lower

legs are hit hardest. Today, muscle data goes to specialists on Earth, who adjust training

from the ground. On the way to Mars, a communication delay of up to 20 minutes makes

that impossible.

How it works:

1. Measure: segmental bioelectrical impedance (BIA) and a tablet-based 3D scan check

individual muscles in about a minute, combined with strength data from the exercise

machine.

2. See: each body part is compared with the person's own baseline and shown on a

green, amber and red body map. The baseline is set after the first two weeks, because

NASA research shows legs shrink early from fluid shift, not only muscle loss. Muscle

loss is flagged only when the scan and strength both drop.

3. Train: transparent rules turn the results into a personal daily plan, weakest muscle

first, with plain-language explanations.

4. Track: progress charts show whether the plan is working.

Motivation: every workout moves the user one step along a game-like journey to Mars

and back home. Milestones unlock video messages from family, recorded before launch.

Benefits and impact: independence from Earth, early detection, personalised training and

stronger motivation. Everything runs offline and data stays on the device. On Earth, the

same approach could help older adults and patients after long bed rest.

Tools: we built the prototype in Lovable (React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS) with local

demo data, and used AI tools for research, design mockups and the pitch.What makes it creative: emotional motivation from family. Factors we considered: comms

delay, fluid shift, privacy, users without medical training, and making health data simple

enough for anyone.
